concern_1_per_traveler_dimension.title: Per-traveler dimension — extend, don't drop
concern_1_per_traveler_dimension.recommendation: EXTEND schemas to formalize per-traveler dimension (Codex's 'half-extension is the disease' wording, Section 8).
rationale: Live evidence: data/china-20260412-092624/modification-log.json:1641-1653 records eight separate edits to fabricated `accommodation_jade` keys across Days 4,7-15 — the field has been re-introduced and re-removed three times across cycles. Half-extension repeatedly snaps back.

Live evidence: spec Section 5.2 A4 documents `passengers_jade`/`booking_status_jade` fabricated on transportation.json Day 12 — same shape (suffix `_jade`), same root cause: schema lacks the dimension.

Live evidence: timeline.schema.json:161-194 has ALREADY taken the extend path (split_day:bool, shared/matilde/jade objects, additionalProperties:false on day_entry). Dropping second-traveler rendering would invalidate that ratified work and erase the Mathilde+Jade scenario the user is actively planning (per Beijing Wudaokou memory).
User context (memory/MEMORY.md): 'Matilde & Jade Trip — 15-day China trip, Jade lives in Beijing Wudaokou'. The two-traveler split-day case is the primary use case, not an edge case.

Codex's binding statement: 'Half-extension is the disease' — partial bolt-on fields keep being fabricated because the schema validates around them. Either commit to the dimension or commit to the single-traveler view.

poi_common.schema.json.rationale: Centralizing the enum allows attractions/meals/entertainment/shopping/cafe to opt in via $ref without each schema redefining.

accommodation_item.add_property_traveler.rationale: Eliminates `accommodation_jade` bolt-on. Day_entry now contains an array of accommodation_item objects, each tagged with traveler. Existing single-accommodation days remain valid because traveler defaults to 'shared'.

accommodation.schema.json.day_entry.shape_change: Replace `accommodation: {$ref: accommodation_item}` with `accommodation: {type: array, items: {$ref: accommodation_item}}`. Backwards-compat: a single-object payload should be auto-wrapped by save.py into a one-element array, OR deprecate single-object writes and run a one-time migration. Recommend the migration path because the auto-wrap reproduces the same dual-format pollution that motivated this spec.
accommodation.schema.json.day_entry.add_split_day: Add `split_day: {type: boolean, default: false}` at day_entry level. additionalProperties:false (see concern 2) prevents fabricated `accommodation_jade` from being written.

location_change.add_property_passengers.rationale: Eliminates `passengers_jade` bolt-on. A flight that only Jade takes is `passengers: ["jade"]`; both travelers is `passengers: ["matilde","jade"]` or `["shared"]`.

transportation.schema.json.day_entry.shape_change: Replace `location_change: {$ref: location_change}` with `location_change: {type: array, items: {$ref: location_change}}`. Same rationale as accommodation: needed when the two travelers take different transports on the same day (spec 5.2 A4 evidence).

timeline.schema.json.status: Already extended (lines 161-194: split_day, shared, matilde, jade). No change required; this is the reference pattern other schemas should match.
timeline.schema.json.minor_consistency_fix: Replace inline `traveler` enum-like block with the new $ref to poi-common's traveler_enum to keep one source of truth.

meals.schema.json_attractions_etc.decision: DEFER per-traveler tagging on these schemas to a follow-up cycle.
meals.schema.json_attractions_etc.rationale: Section 5.2 bug accounting (A6, A7, A9-A12) shows that meals/attractions/entertainment/shopping fabrications were location-confusion (Wudaokou vs Xi'an) rather than per-traveler split. Adding traveler:enum here without evidence creates the very 'fabricated bolt-on' Codex warned against. Re-evaluate ONLY if a second cycle reproduces split-day fabrications on those POI types.

concern_3_renderer_consistency.title: Renderer consistency — pick path B (cache as sole source)
concern_3_renderer_consistency.recommendation: PATH B: image_url is NEVER written into agent JSON; cache (data/<trip>/images.json) is the single source of truth.
rationale: Live evidence: scripts/generate-html-interactive.py inconsistently honors `item.image_url`. Honored at lines 715 (cafe), 832 (shopping), 938 (accommodation). IGNORED at lines 669/1308 (meals), 756 (attractions), 802 (entertainment) — those branches go straight to `_get_placeholder_image` which reads images.json. So even if image_url is written, half the renderer ignores it.

Live evidence: data/china-20260412-092624/{meals,attractions,entertainment,cafe,shopping,accommodation}.json contain 134 image_url fields total (counts: meals 64, attractions 34, entertainment 13, accommodation 10, shopping 10, cafe 3). Each one is a redundant copy of a value already in images.json — and each one is a NEW vector for a `key=AIzaSy...` URL leak. Path A would multiply the leak surface 134x; path B keeps it bounded to images.json.

Live evidence: TWO write paths exist for image_url into agent JSON: (a) scripts/fetch-images-batch.py:1166-1334 writes via raw `json.dump` (line 1334) — bypassing scripts/lib/json_io.save_agent_json validation entirely; (b) scripts/save.py:65-101 (`extract_image_urls` → `_fetch_poi_image` → `poi['image_url'] = photo_url` line 75) — invoked unconditionally on every save (line 574). Both paths must be removed under path B.

Codex Top-5 control 4 binding requirement: 'No agent (any type) may directly write image_url field; images go through scripts/fetch-images-batch.py only.' Path A (renderer honors image_url for ALL POI types) would require keeping the image_url field as a valid schema property; path B removes it from the schema and from the data, which is strictly easier to enforce.
Path B aligns with the existing `_get_placeholder_image()` cache lookup which is already implemented for all POI categories (lines 272-339).

Line 938 — same simplification for accommodation. The other call sites (669, 756, 802, 1308, 1336) already do this — they become consistent.

The corresponding image fetch should be a separate, explicit `python scripts/fetch-images-batch.py` invocation (already the canonical, per `.claude/commands/review.md` lines 510-540).

The information is recoverable from images.json (or refetchable). 134 fields removed across the live trip. After strip, schema flip in concern_2 will block re-introduction.

Path A keeps the dual write paths (fetch-images-batch + save.py extract_image_urls), and the spec's Top-5 control 4 forbids agents writing image_url at all. Path A makes the lock harder, not easier.

concern_4_verifier_integration_point.title: verify-plan-integrity.py integration point in generate-and-deploy.sh
concern_4_verifier_integration_point.recommendation: Insert a new Step 1.5 (renumber subsequent steps to [2.5/6] etc., or use an explicit '[VERIFY]' tag) AFTER image fetch (current line 154) and BEFORE HTML generation (current line 156-159).

exact_insertion_point.current_line_154_content: echo ""  (blank line that ends the image-fetch block)
shape_of_inserted_block: echo -e "${RED}DEPLOY BLOCKED: plan integrity verifier failed (exit $VERIFY_EXIT)${NC}"

rationale: Verifier must run AFTER image fetch because checks include (per spec 5.2 control 1): 'Stock-image-URL grep' and 'HTTP-protocol grep on image_url' — those checks are meaningful only against the post-fetch state of images.json + agent JSON.

Verifier must run BEFORE HTML generation (line 159) so a failed verify aborts before deploy-relevant artifacts are produced. Spec 5.2 control 1 wording: 'Called by: scripts/generate-and-deploy.sh BEFORE HTML generation'.

The HTML-rendered scan (last item in Codex's 6-in-1 verifier) requires a SECOND invocation AFTER line 168 (post-generation, pre-deploy line 184). The single-script approach is to expose two CLI modes: `verify-plan-integrity.py <plan-id>` (data-only) and `verify-plan-integrity.py <plan-id> --html-also <output-file>` (data + rendered HTML). Recommend the orchestrator dispatch invokes the data mode at line 155 and the html mode at line 168.5.

Per Section 5.2 user-accept clause (5.1), the API-key grep `key=AIzaSy[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}` runs in WARN mode only — verifier emits a yellow notice but exits 0 for that check alone. All other checks (forbidden tokens, stock URLs, http://, schema) exit non-zero on FAIL.

The retry helper `fetch_images_with_retry` (lines 88-117) wraps image-fetch failures and continues the pipeline with `IMAGE_FETCH_STATUS=FAILED`. The verifier MUST detect this state and abort even if the helper returned 0 — recommend exporting `IMAGE_FETCH_STATUS` and having verify-plan-integrity.py read it as an env signal.
concern_4_verifier_integration_point.anti_pattern_to_avoid: Do NOT call verify-plan-integrity.py from within plan-validate.py or json_io.py (write-time hook). The verifier is a deploy gate, not a write gate — write-time validation is concern_2's job. Mixing them produces the 'hook stack' Codex rejected (HK-11).

concern_6_agent_ownership_owned_files_re.title: Per-agent owned_files regex shape + pretool-write hook integration

owned_files_field_shape.value: YAML list of regex strings (Python `re` flavor, anchored — pattern is implicitly ^...$ on the repo-relative path).
owned_files_field_shape.rationale: Regex (not glob) because the patterns must distinguish e.g. `data/.+/meals\.json` from `data/.+/meals\.json\.bak` and need character-class precision.

shared_writer_modification_log.issue: modification-log.json is written by every agent (per existing review.md and agent files prescribing `python scripts/log-modification.py`).
shared_writer_modification_log.resolution: All agents legitimately own modification-log.json; the regex appears in every agent's owned_files list. Hook implementation: a path is allowed if ANY active agent's owned_files regex matches.

global_universal_deny.rationale: Codex Top-5 control 4: 'No agent (any type) may directly write image_url'. Implementation: pretool-write hook scans the proposed JSON payload BEFORE write, rejects if the diff introduces an `image_url` key on any object that previously didn't have one or that has a different value. Match by Python json walker, not regex on raw text (safer with embedded quotes/newlines).
global_universal_deny.exception: scripts/fetch-images-batch.py (system tool, runs as user/orchestrator, NOT as agent) — but per concern_3 path B, fetch-images-batch.py is also forbidden from writing image_url into agent JSON; the only writer of image_url is data/<trip>/images.json which has no image_url field, only `pois: {key: url}`. So the universal deny becomes a clean 'no agent and no script writes image_url anywhere except images.json'.

hook_integration_point.hook_file: Single hook: ~/.claude/hooks/pretool-write.py (or whatever the existing pretool-write hook is named for this project — verify before extending).
behavior: 1. If agent_id is unset (orchestrator), skip — orchestrator is governed by the orchestrator-gate hook.
2. Look up the calling subagent's `owned_files` from .claude/agents/<agent>.md frontmatter.
3. Check target path against owned_files regex list. If no match → exit 2 with diagnostic.
4. Additionally: parse JSON body, walk for `image_url` keys; if any found → exit 2 with diagnostic (this is the universal deny).
5. Cache parsed frontmatter for the session; bust cache on .claude/agents/*.md mtime change.
hook_integration_point.extends_not_creates: Reuse the existing orchestrator-gate / safety hook scaffolding; do NOT add a 30-hook stack. This is a single new check inside one existing hook.

anti_patterns_to_avoid: Do NOT define owned_files as a glob list (e.g. 'data/**/meals.json'). Glob doesn't anchor and bak files would slip through.
Do NOT make the universal-deny a separate hook (Codex REJECTED 'one hook per symptom'). It's one extra check in the same pretool-write hook.
Do NOT permit agents to write to images.json. fetch-images-batch.py is the sole writer; that script is invoked by the orchestrator/user, not by an agent dispatch.
Do NOT enforce owned_files via the prompt-purity hook — that hook checks orchestrator dispatch text; this hook checks the actual filesystem write.

architecture_proposals.title: Single source of truth for image data: cache only (path B)
architecture_proposals.current_state: Three independent write paths populate image_url: (a) scripts/fetch-images-batch.py:1166-1334 raw json.dump; (b) scripts/save.py:65-101 inline fetch+write on every save; (c) any agent that ignores the WRITE-FORBIDDEN section. Renderer honors image_url for 3 POI types (cafe/shopping/accommodation), ignores it for 4 (meals/attractions/entertainment + duplicate accommodation site). 134 image_url fields in current trip data, each a copy of an images.json entry. Each is also a leak vector for unsplash/http/key=AIzaSy (E6, E7, E8 in spec).
architecture_proposals.proposed_state: image_url removed from all schemas and from all agent data. Sole image source is data/<trip>/images.json (already populated by fetch-images-batch.py:227). Renderer reads images.json via existing _get_placeholder_image() (lines 272-339), which already covers all POI categories. Agents may not write image_url under any circumstance (universal-deny in pretool-write hook).
architecture_proposals.measurable_benefit: Eliminates 134 redundant fields from current trip data (and proportionally more on other trips). Reduces image-leak surface from 134+1 sites to 1 site (images.json). Removes 3 of 3 write paths, leaving 1. Removes ~50 lines from save.py, ~240 lines from fetch-images-batch.py, ~5 schema fields, simplifies renderer to a single uniform code path.
architecture_proposals.risk_if_ignored: Future agent dispatch with mistaken image_url (or copy-pasted from a previous cycle) re-introduces the 'fabricated bolt-on' anti-pattern. Each new trip multiplies the leak surface. The renderer's split behavior means image bugs surface on half the categories and are masked on the other half — same false-PASS pattern as the cycle 123425 placeholder regression.
architecture_proposals.migration_strategy: Stage 1: strip image_url from all current data files (one-time script). Stage 2: simplify renderer (3 line changes). Stage 3: remove extract_image_urls block from save.py (50 lines). Stage 4: remove agent-JSON write block from fetch-images-batch.py (240 lines). Stage 5: remove image_url from 6 schemas. Stage 6: flip additionalProperties:false (concern 2) — at this point the schema enforces non-rewriting. Each stage independently passes the existing validators.

architecture_proposals.title: Per-traveler dimension as first-class schema concept
architecture_proposals.current_state: schema/timeline.schema.json:161-194 has the dimension formally (split_day, shared, matilde, jade); accommodation.schema.json and transportation.schema.json do not. Result: every multi-traveler cycle re-fabricates `accommodation_jade`/`passengers_jade`/`booking_status_jade` at day-level (Section 5.2 A2, A4, A6). modification-log.json:1638-1689 records three full add-then-remove cycles across the same fields.
architecture_proposals.proposed_state: poi-common.schema.json adds `traveler_enum` ($defs). accommodation_item gains `traveler` field (default 'shared'). day_entry's accommodation field becomes an array (one item per traveler). Same for transportation: location_change gains `passengers` array; day_entry's location_change becomes an array. day_entry adds `split_day:bool`. additionalProperties:false on day_entry rejects fabricated `_jade` suffixes.
architecture_proposals.measurable_benefit: Eliminates a recurring failure class (3 documented re-fabrication cycles → 0). Gives the renderer a uniform traveler dimension to consume, replacing ad hoc `_inject_intra_routes` band-aid (spec Section 1, deferred defect 8) which exists precisely because the data shape is ambiguous.
architecture_proposals.risk_if_ignored: Section 8 ('Half-extension is the disease') comes due again next cycle: a new variant of `accommodation_jade` will appear. The orchestrator's prompt-purity hook is warning-only (Section 1, deferred defect 4) so it cannot block.
architecture_proposals.migration_strategy: Stage 1: write the schema changes alongside a `scripts/migrate-traveler-dimension.py` that converts day_entry.accommodation: {} → day_entry.accommodation: [{...,traveler:'shared'}] and folds existing accommodation_jade into a second array element with traveler:'jade'. Stage 2: run the migration on china-20260412-092624 (the only multi-traveler trip in current data) and validate that the rendered output is unchanged. Stage 3: ship the schema flip + renderer update together. Stage 4: the additionalProperties:false flip from concern 2 then permanently locks out the bolt-on pattern.

architecture_proposals.title: Single deploy verifier with two CLI modes (data + html), no hook stack
architecture_proposals.current_state: No verifier exists. scripts/generate-and-deploy.sh runs image fetch → HTML generate → deploy without an integrity gate. Per Codex audit the live trip has 27 schema validation failures + 13 warnings that would block a verified deploy but do not block this script.
architecture_proposals.proposed_state: scripts/verify-plan-integrity.py with two modes: `verify-plan-integrity.py <plan-id>` (data-only: schema validation, forbidden-token grep on data, stock-image grep, http:// grep, key=AIzaSy WARN-only grep) and `verify-plan-integrity.py <plan-id> --html-also <output-file>` (the above PLUS forbidden-token grep on the rendered HTML). generate-and-deploy.sh invokes mode 1 between current lines 154 and 156, mode 2 between current lines 168 and 184.
architecture_proposals.measurable_benefit: Replaces the 30+ rejected bespoke hooks with one script. Catches all 6 documented failure classes from spec 5.2 control 1 in one place. Mode 1 fails fast (before HTML gen), mode 2 catches renderer-introduced regressions (e.g. C1-C10 band-aid effects). One file to maintain, one CLI to learn.
architecture_proposals.risk_if_ignored: Each future cycle re-discovers a subset of the same checks ad hoc, the way cycles 123425 and 174743 re-discovered placeholder regression three times before AC2 grep alternations were complete. Without one canonical gate, 'PASS' verdicts diverge across subagents.
architecture_proposals.migration_strategy: Stage 1: implement the script using existing scripts/plan-validate.py (already running 27-failures detection per Section 1). Stage 2: wire into generate-and-deploy.sh with a temporary `--allow-existing-failures` flag during the data-cleanup window (concern_2 Stage A). Stage 3: remove the flag after data is clean. Stage 4: reuse the script's data-mode as the source-of-truth check in subagent acceptance reports (Codex Top-5 control 5).
